default_prompt: You are screening a record for a systematic review on longitudinal trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms. Read the title and abstract and decide whether the record should be included, applying this review's published eligibility criteria (SYNERGY dataset; original review DOI 10.1080/00273171.2017.1412293): the study must be a longitudinal study with at least three measurement waves measuring PTSD; PTSD must be measured on a continuous scale via an interview or questionnaire; the study must use a clustering method (LGMM, LCGA, or hierarchical cluster analysis); and the traumatic stress symptoms must follow events that appeared to fulfill DSM-IV criterion A1 for PTSD or acute stress disorder.
_notes: x = 4, four distinct vendor families: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral.
The Mistral vendor requires the attest[mistral] extra (mistralai>=1.0),
already included in attest[all]; needs MISTRAL_API_KEY.
tau was 0.75 before this fix, which is inert: with x = 4 and votes in
{-1, 0, 1}, the maximum sample standard deviation (n-1 denominator)
any non-boundary vote vector can reach is ~0.577, from an even 2-2
split such as (1,1,0,0) -- any vector mixing a -1 and a +1 is already
caught by the boundary indicator, not the dispersion term. So
tau = 0.75 could never fire the dispersion criterion and escalation
silently reduced to the boundary rule alone. tau is now 0.5: a 2-2
split has s = sqrt(1/3) ~= 0.577 > 0.5 and escalates, while a 3-1
majority such as (1,1,1,0) has s = 0.5, which is not > tau, so it
still auto-labels. tau is a pre-specified, logged part of this
configuration -- see
attest.ensemble.aggregate.dispersion/_boundary_dispersion.
Model pinning (2026-08-02): mistral-large-latest was a floating alias
and has been replaced with the pinned mistral-large-2512. anthropic's
claude-sonnet-5 is left as-is: per Anthropic's model-ID documentation,
dateless IDs from the Claude 4.6 generation onward are themselves
pinned snapshots, not evergreen pointers, so this is not a floating
alias. openai's gpt-4o and google's gemini-2.0-flash are both
bare/floating family names (and gemini-2.0-flash was reportedly
retired 2026-06-01, per vendor docs) -- neither could be resolved to
a specific dated snapshot from documentation alone in this pass, so
both are left as explicit TODO markers in 'model' rather than
silently kept as floating aliases. Resolve both TODOs against each
vendor's current model list before the real run.
Tier mismatch: gpt-4o and gemini-2.0-flash are an older capability
generation than claude-sonnet-5 and mistral-large-2512, which would
confound 'vendor' with 'model tier' in the inter-vendor agreement and
leave-one-out ablation. This is not a deliberate mix -- the TODOs
above are to pin openai and google to their current-generation
flagships specifically, closing the tier gap, not just to any dated
snapshot.
model_version values are 'TODO:capture-served-snapshot-before-freeze'.
Replace each with the exact dated snapshot the vendor's API confirms
it served (many vendors echo this back in the response) before

This requires a live API call per vendor and could not be done in

default_prompt (was track_prompts, migrated 2026-08-17) is what the kernel
actually reads to screen every record: attest.provenance.config.Config.
prompt_for_track falls back to default_prompt for any record whose track
has no track_prompts entry -- and since 2026-08-17 this file carries no
track_prompts at all, so every record in a run gets this one prompt,
regardless of its track field. This is deliberate, not a regression: the
runbook now proves attest's core mechanism (read title/abstract, apply one
instruction, four vendors vote, decide escalate-or-not) by running the
whole pipeline independently once per SYNERGY review -- one list, one
prompt per run -- rather than pooling multiple reviews' different
eligibility questions into one run via track_prompts routing. See
README §6 for why: the reviews are different screening questions
(different domains, different criteria), not repeats of the same
measurement, so a multi-track pooled run was never the right design.
To run against a different review: replace default_prompt's text below
(and reviews.toml's review name, by hand, in the same commit/edit) --
criteria text for every review this repo has already vetted is kept
ready to paste back in, verbatim, lightly reflowed to prose, from each
review's eligibility_criteria field in asreview/synergy-dataset's
datasets.toml (re-verify against that file if it's been a while):
Appenzeller-Herzog_2019 -- "You are screening a record for a systematic
review on drug treatments for Wilson's disease. Read the title and
abstract and decide whether the record should be included, applying this
review's published eligibility criteria (SYNERGY dataset; original review
DOI 10.1111/liv.14179): patients with Wilson's disease (WD) of any age or
stage; the study drug must be one of four established therapies
(D-penicillamine, trientine, TTM, or zinc); the control/comparator must
not include the study drug itself (e.g. placebo, no treatment, or a
different one of the four therapies), with matched doses across arms;
concomitant therapies must be identical across the compared arms;
comparisons between a monotherapy and a combination regimen that
includes that same monotherapy drug (e.g. D-penicillamine plus zinc vs.
zinc alone) are excluded, not merely out of scope; the study must report
at least one of all-cause mortality, orthotopic liver transplantation,
neurological symptoms, liver-related symptoms, adverse effects, or
frequency of treatment discontinuation; and the study must be a
prospective or retrospective study, including randomized,
non-randomized controlled trials or comparative observational studies,
in English, German, Dutch, French, Spanish, or Portuguese. Exclude
animal studies, case reports, case series, cross-sectional studies,
before-after studies, reviews, letters, abstract-only publications,
editorials, diagnostic or other testing studies, and non-controlled
studies."
Muthu_2021 -- "You are screening a record for a systematic review of
randomized controlled trials on perioperative variables in spine surgery.
Read the title and abstract and decide whether the record should be
included, applying this review's published eligibility criteria (SYNERGY
dataset; original review DOI 10.1097/BRS.0000000000003645): the study
must be an RCT with a 1:1 parallel two-arm design; related to spine
surgery involving preoperative, intraoperative, or postoperative
variables; and have a dichotomous primary or secondary outcome. Exclude
studies not involving human subjects, studies with continuous-variable
outcomes (e.g. pain scores, Oswestry Disability Index scores, time to
union) without predefined clinical success criteria, and studies that
did not report a statistically significant primary or secondary outcome
measure."
prompt_version bumped v2 -> v3 (2026-08-03, predates the track_prompts ->
default_prompt migration but the reasoning still applies): the prompt
used to end with its own 'Respond with exactly one token: -1 to exclude,
0 if related but uncertain, or 1 to include.' sentence. The kernel now
owns the output-format contract outright --
attest.vendors.base.compose_system_prompt appends its own
OUTPUT_CONTRACT to every criteria string on every rater path (sync,
batch, and DeterministicRater), and warns if the supplied criteria
already contains a copy of it. So the trailing sentence must never be
added back to default_prompt or any of the criteria text above, or the
composed prompt ships that instruction twice and trips the kernel's
warning on every screen run. prompt_version is still a provenance label
only (not read back by the kernel -- see attest.provenance.config.
VendorSpec), so keep it bumped by hand with any future prompt change.
zero_policy (added 2026-08-03, explicit here though 'escalate' is the
loader's own default -- attest.cli._load_ensemble_config /
attest.provenance.config.Config both default to it) governs the one
case g's boundary+dispersion rule used to auto-label without
escalating: a non-boundary vote vector whose mean lands exactly on 0
(e.g. all-uncertain). Ordinal 0 has no place in the gold-binary
confusion matrix, so that used to silently become a fabricated false
negative or false positive downstream. Decision.auto_label can no
longer be 0 at all: under 'escalate' (kept here, the recall-safe
choice) a would-be 0 routes to human adjudication like any other
escalation; the only alternative is 'include' (folds it into +1) --
there is deliberately no 'exclude' option, since that's the one
disposition that would silently destroy recall. See
attest.ensemble.aggregate.g/_boundary_dispersion. This repo's
src/score_audit.py was audited against the kernel's migration note for
this change (it only maps drawn record ids to SYNERGY gold labels for
audit-apply and never itself branches on a predicted/auto label), so
no dead predicted-0 branch was found there to remove.
tau is no longer only hand-verified: attest.ensemble.tau.validate_tau
now runs automatically at `attest screen` epoch-open time against this
tau and the derived x, and the proof is persisted to
data/run/tau_report.json and re-surfaced under 'tau_report' in
validate's output -- so the 0.5-for-x=4 reasoning below is now
cross-checked by the kernel itself on every run, not just at config-
authoring time. `attest ablate` takes the same tau at face value
across the whole x-sweep (see the Makefile's TAU var and README §5
step 7); because the attainable-dispersion set depends on x, one
fixed tau is not behaviorally comparable in strength across the
swept subset sizes x' < 4 -- xsweep attaches each subset's own
describe_tau() to the ablation report and warns once per sweep about
this, which is expected and does not need a config change.
tau (updated 2026-08-03) is set via
attest.ensemble.tau.resolve_tau("escalate_ties", x=4), the canonical
midpoint of the escalate-ties regime at x=4 -- must be recomputed if x
changes, since tau is not comparable across ensemble sizes.
temperature (added 2026-08-05, required as of kernel commit ab9cdef):
attest.provenance.config.VendorSpec gained a required 'temperature'
field with no default -- _load_ensemble_config reads spec['temperature']
directly, so a vendor entry missing it now raises KeyError at load time
instead of silently doing nothing. Set to 0.0 (deterministic sampling)
on all four vendors here, matching the kernel's own data/example_config.json
convention for a screening task where reproducibility matters more than
response diversity. Unlike model_version/prompt_version, temperature is
now actually sent as the live sampling parameter (previously unversioned
and unset, i.e. each vendor's own API default) -- this is a first-time
behavior pin, not just a provenance label. It is hash-sensitive: adding
it here changes ensemble_config_id and opens a new epoch, same as any
model_version/prompt_version change would.
Same kernel commit (ab9cdef) also started enforcing model_version
against what each vendor's own response reports, raising
ModelVersionDriftError on mismatch (skipped only for Google, whose
response doesn't expose it). The four 'TODO:capture-served-snapshot-
before-freeze' placeholders above are therefore no longer just
documentation debt -- anthropic/openai/mistral will hard-fail on the
very first live call until each is replaced with the exact snapshot
string that vendor's API actually reports. Resolve before the next
live run.
confidence_threshold (added 2026-08-05, optional, default 0.5): set
explicitly here purely for clarity -- attest.cli._load_ensemble_config
already falls back to attest.ensemble.confidence.DEFAULT_LOW_THRESHOLD
(also 0.5) when this key is absent, so this is a no-op behaviorally,
not a fix. It's the default 'low_threshold' a confidence-stratified
audit-draw uses when its own --confidence-threshold flag isn't passed.
Unlike temperature, this is deliberately excluded from to_dict()/
ensemble_config_id (attest.provenance.config.Config docstring) -- it
changes only how an already-fixed excluded population is stratified
for audit, never what a vendor samples or the ensemble's aggregate
decision, so setting or changing it does not open a new epoch.

actual datasets.toml from GitHub (not just trusted the earlier paraphrase)

itself be revised upstream.
This file is not read literally beyond 'vendors' (including each
vendor's 'temperature'), 'aggregation', 'tau', 'zero_policy',
'default_prompt', 'track_prompts' (unused here since the 2026-08-17
migration above, but still a valid field if a future pooled run ever
needs it again), and 'confidence_threshold' (see
attest.cli._load_ensemble_config) -- this _notes field is ignored by
the loader and safe to keep as documentation.
